title: Sudoku Solver
tagline: Fill empty cells with constraint-checked guesses, backtracking on contradictions.

intuition.analogy: Solving a Sudoku by hand: you pencil a candidate into an empty cell, continue solving, and if you hit an impossible cell you erase back to your last guess and try a different number.
paragraphs: Sudoku is constraint satisfaction: each empty cell needs a digit 1–9 such that its row, column, and 3×3 box stay free of duplicates. Backtracking tries candidates and recurses, undoing choices that lead to dead ends.
Efficiency comes from constant-time validity checks. Maintain bitmasks (or sets) of used digits per row, per column, and per box, so testing a candidate is O(1) instead of scanning 27 cells.

Smart move ordering — always fill the empty cell with the fewest legal candidates first (the 'most constrained variable' heuristic) — slashes the search dramatically, often solving puzzles almost instantly.
intuition.keyIdea: Guess a digit, check row/col/box constraints in O(1), recurse, and erase on contradiction.

steps.title: Find an empty cell
steps.detail: Optionally choose the one with the fewest candidates (most-constrained-variable heuristic).

steps.title: Try candidates
steps.detail: For each digit not in the cell's row, column, or box, place it, update the masks, and recurse.

steps.title: Backtrack
steps.detail: If recursion fails, remove the digit and clear the masks, then try the next candidate. Success when no empty cells remain.

complexity.time: Exponential worst case, fast with pruning
complexity.timeReason: The branching is bounded by candidates per cell; good heuristics keep it tiny in practice.

pitfalls: O(1) validity via row/col/box masks is the key optimisation — naive rescanning is slow.
Don't forget to clear the cell (and masks) when backtracking.
Box index is (r/3)*3 + c/3 — a common off-by-one source.

dryRun.clickMoment: The first guess (3) cascades into an impossible cell deeper down; backtracking rewinds exactly to this decision and the alternative (7) succeeds. The recursion remembers the choice point for you.
